problemH: Every grey wheelie bin looks the same. Yours included.
problemP: The wheelie bin sits right at the front of the drive – it's the first thing people see. Grey plastic, a house number scrawled on in marker pen, and identical to next door's, so after collection day you're still lifting the lid to work out which one's yours.
losningH: The fix: four faces, four bins with their own personality
losningP: One winking and cackling, one poking its tongue out, one grinning ear to ear – and one crying about being the wheelie bin. Press one onto each bin and you'll spot yours from the front door, and the bin everyone pretends not to have becomes the funniest thing on the street.
bullets: Spot your bin from the front door – four different faces: winking and cackling, tongue out, big grin and crying
Rain and grime wipe off with a cloth – smooth PVC surface with no texture for dirt to sit in
Goes on by hand, straight onto the bin – self-adhesive backing, no tools and no glue needed
Sits flat with no bubbling at the edges – flat 2D print that follows the shape of the bin
Covers the whole row of bins – four sheets at 20 × 20 cm (7.9 × 7.9 in), or stick them on the fridge, doors and cupboard fronts
